best_parts: node grade_vignette: Ravi vignette with two TR8 traps (WBC 14,000 under the routine-flag reflex, 20 h pain against the 24 h line) and a Grade I key; each wrong option names a wrong model and carries a sure_note
node fit_retest: TR11 retested in a new form (home on antibiotics, return in 6-8 weeks) with a correct same-admission surgery option, after the earlier TR11 probes
node grade_ok: skip lane ('I know the grades, skip the criteria') offered only after a correct answer, so the fast lane follows evidence of mastery
flaws: node retest_t10 and fit_retest option 'Drain the gallbladder and book surgery later': mapped to TR10 (early surgery in every grade), but it is a drain-first-in-a-fit-patient model; the mapping is loose for the report
node unfit_seq: the key is the only option without a cholecystectomy, and the stem already says 'unfit', so the key is findable by form (DP1)
node grade_t8b: 20 hours against a 24-hour distractor is a weak temptation; a learner holding the wrong model would rarely choose it

best_parts: node t11b_t1 'Show me why' to t11_case: a contrast of Patient A (operated this admission) and Patient B (antibiotics, date in 6-8 weeks) is a different second explanation from the rule-based one
node t11b_why: 'PYQs kept the older wait, which is why the same stem can carry two keys' is a precise teach-both line for exam readers
node g1 and g3: TR8 in two forms (numbers, then a Grade I vignette with creatinine 1.8 that tests the 1.5 trap in context) with sure_notes naming the routine-lab reflex
flaws: node enter skip path ('Yes, test me') goes straight to the single g3 probe, so the Grade II and Grade III cut-offs are never taught or tested on that path (O7 depth thin)
node g3: the correct option 'Grade I, since it meets neither II nor III' is the only option without a number, so it can be found by form (DP1)
node t10b: the two distractors carry absolute words ('at once', 'every patient') that the key lacks; a tired student can pick the key by that cue (DP1)

best_parts: node key: an exam-form probe ('Exam question: ... by current standards?') with an explicit teach-both key_ok ('Older PYQs expected the interval route...')
node g3_t_inr: the INR distractor is explained by the wrong model (warfarin reflex) and refuted with the TG18 hepatic bar
node vig: a Grade III vignette (noradrenaline, creatinine 3.1) whose wrong options name the operate-first reflex
flaws: node why: the key 'Surgery is unsafe while organs fail; support and drain first' is the longest option and the only one with a semicolon, so it is findable by form; it also repeats the answer shown one node earlier (DP1, weak diagnosticity)
node open through g3: no probe asks the learner to assign a grade from a vignette (Grade I is never a key), so O7 'assign TG18 grade' is only partly met
whole segment: no fast lane or skip, and no wrong-answer branch offers a second explanation ('Show me why' absent), so every error gets the same single route with 'Try again'

merge_ideas: a's grade_vignette and skip lane, with b's t11_case contrast as the second explanation after a TR11 miss
b's enter bridge, but with a's graded vignette (Ravi-style) so the skip learner still meets a Grade II and a Grade III probe
c's exam-form key probe with teach-both key_ok placed before a's fit_retest, so exam wording is drilled before the cold retest
c's vig Grade III vignette added to a's grade section, so every path tests the operate-first reflex in a sick patient
